title: Shift-left affected validation with reusable execution evidence

statements.text: For trigger edit or affected, the repository adapter's select returns the checks whose owned path patterns match a changed path and every check that depends on them, and reports an affected basis with an incomplete selection.

Trigger affected is an explicit request for the affected selection including expensive checks. The triggers edit, checkpoint and manual keep their meaning, and a checkpoint still selects the complete obligation.

A changed path that no component owns, or a change under the workflow directory, to the adapter, the ownership table, a dependency lockfile, the project manifest or shared test infrastructure, selects the broad or complete obligation.

Each repository keeps exactly one ownership table. This repository declares no lifecycle CI mapping, so the adapter's component table is its only instance, and a repository test requires any later CI mapping to repeat its identifiers and path patterns.

Selection is one function of the snapshot, the pinned base and the ownership table. The enrolled runner, the managed owner, the plan command and the run command all use it, and a check outside the derived selection refuses.

A check is eligible only on lanes where the repository's hosted matrix executes it. The instruction and full pytest checks become Linux-native, and the macOS-only Swift check retires with the Linux cutover.
A lane the host cannot provide is a classified unavailable result. Nothing is substituted, emulated or inferred to pass.

Dagger is an optional executor and the backend already classifies it: a Dagger check runs on a configured reachable engine with the pinned identity and is otherwise unavailable with an existing classified code. This Initiative pins each outcome with a regression, and the runner never installs, starts or configures a container engine.

The managed owner implements a validate action that runs the affected selection for an enrolled open task on a fresh immutable snapshot under the existing host admission and returns observation references.
The managed owner implements an applicability action that reports whether a recorded snapshot still matches the worktree under the runner's existing source-freshness rule, with the changed paths.
Execution stays default-off. It requires an enabled enrollment for the exact worktree and task, installs no watcher, service or login item, and sends no feedback without the separate existing opt-in.
The adapter exposes plan and run commands that need only the checkout, Python and uv, so hosted CI and people use the same selection without DBSCTR.
No automatic test splitting, no selector rewrite in consumer repositories, no change to required hosted checks and no speed claim without a measurement.
Validation starts on settled edits inside the open cycle. Commits stay gate-driven and pushes stay delivery-driven, so the forge queue is not on the per-edit path.
Path-aware selection can miss a test that a changed file affects. The conservative fallback, the full hosted suite and the shadow comparison keep misses visible.
Early validation on the developer host competes with foreground work. The existing host admission, the checkpoint rule for expensive checks and opt-out apply unchanged.

dbsctrctl validate runs the affected selection inside an open cycle before any commit, stores one execution receipt per executed result, reports failing test identities, and changes no gate, exception, counter or Gate Commit.
dbsctrctl reference-evidence records a gate's own reference item to an existing passing execution instead of a second execution, and never alters the original.

A reference is admitted only under fail-closed rules: the execution passed, was not superseded by a later non-passing execution of the same check on the same content, still matches the worktree in its scope, lies under the current Initiative authority and satisfies the existing predecessor rule. An evidence item recorded at another head is referenceable only through a retained binding; a receipt is referenceable at any head while its captured content is unchanged.

Under an approved evidence policy a reference inherits the execution's binding only when the referencing gate's declaration is identical to the declaration the execution was recorded under. Coverage and the gate policy digest are recomputed for that gate.

Gate decisions stay separate. The rerun-invalidation transition policy, gate order, the signatures and error strings of record-evidence, set-gate and Gate Commit, and existing record schemas are unchanged, and set-gate still refuses another gate's evidence identifier.

dbsctrctl evidence-plan reports without mutating which executions each gate can reference and which selected checks are missing or stale, and validate executes only the missing or stale checks. The managed validation owner supplies read-only affected selection on settled edits, receipt metadata from the completed request, and snapshot path membership. The lifecycle does not read the runner's private store.
dbsctrctl evidence-export writes a validation manifest for one committed head from the executions admissible at that head. Publishing it is a separate explicit operator action.

A receipt comes only from an execution the lifecycle requested. Imported files, adapter output, JUnit and forge checks are never receipts, and local evidence is exactly as trustworthy as the account that records it.

Unreferenced receipts are bounded per cycle, a receipt that any evidence item references is retained as history, and an amendment that reopens a gate makes earlier executions non-referenceable for it.

A wrong reference could pass a gate on stale or narrower evidence than its obligation. Fail-closed admissibility, declaration identity under policy, a regression per refusal and unchanged union validation on an advanced base mitigate it.

One separate report-only workflow adds an affected job that runs the repository's affected selection on a hosted Linux runner for each pull request, so the cloud path gives early feedback when local compute is unavailable.
Its compare job runs after the required test workflow completes and reports per check and test group would_reuse, would_reuse_if_lane_equivalent or must_run, with a reason for each must_run group.

The report separates queue time, worker wall time, the repeated early-selection step and the summary tail, counts identical test identities executed more than once on the same source and runtime, and never estimates a missing value.
The validation manifest travels as a Git note on the validated head commit, which changes neither tree nor commit and needs no repository setting. It is untrusted input.

The shadow changes no conclusion of the required workflow, required check, permission or artifact. It uses a read-only token and no secret, writes nothing to the pull request, and a missing or malformed manifest reports unavailable while the job succeeds.
A local execution can replace hosted execution only when lane identity matches or the repository declares a lane policy. The report shows both counts separately and grants nothing.
The required workflow retains no lane identity beyond the Python and Worktrunk versions, so strict reuse reports lane_unverified until that workflow retains it.
ARM64 workstation executions cannot stand in for x86_64 hosted lanes. Replacement needs a matching lane or a declared lane policy, so hosted savings are unknown until the shadow measures them.
Late hosted controls keep gating merge and never gate agent feedback. Their results return through the existing integration coordinator, whose activation stays with its own Initiative.
The private consumer repository is not changed. It works without DBSCTR, keeps its own selector, and any CI refactor there follows the results of this shadow as a separate decision.
Affected selection replaces broader local repetition only while the repository's configured full CI stays authoritative for repository-wide compatibility.

Unmerged local drafts are reconciled rather than rebased. The gate-aware draft's purpose and cadence model and executor kinds are carried here, its macOS controller and Lima executor are retired with the macOS workstation, and the VM-resident owner kind remains its own delivery.
Authoritative hosted reuse through a trusted producer, including replacing a required check, is deferred until the shadow shows eligible volume and the trust decision is approved.

Mirroring repositories to a self-hosted forge, forge projects or a kanban board for planning and agent observability are deferred. PM Kernel owns local tickets, and mirroring a client repository needs the client's permission.

Non-goals: changing branch protections or enterprise settings, automatic merge from a local manifest, automatic watchers or services, concurrency activation, and changing the serial order of dbsctr-cycle-speed.
